content:
marco (partnerships): heads up — CloudVendor wants to publicize the joint marketplace listing next Tue at 09:00 PT. their marketplace PO shows 8 racks reserved but vendor just sent a manifest with only 4 assigned. :eyes:
sara (procurement): wait, 4? our committed reservation for Dedicated customers is 8 racks for Q2. where did the other 4 go?
devon (logistics): carrier update: one container from OR dock hit customs delay, ETA slipped 6 days. manifest snippet from vendor: ```PO: CV-78910\nassigned_racks: 4\nshipment_id: CNTR-3344\neta: 2026-03-31```
marco (partnerships): that kills the demo capacity for the marketplace preview — CloudVendor expects us to demo live on their listing. can we short-term reassign from another marketplace pool?
sara (procurement): checking current pool allocations now. quick status: Dedicated pool EU has 2 spare racks, APAC none, Hosted spare capacity is warm but not guaranteed for reserved SKU.
li (eng-ml): from an ML runtime POV we can run smaller-scale demos by sharding across hosts but SLA/perf won't match the Certified Dedicated SKU; would need to call it out in announce copy.
ops-bot: [deploy-check] reserved-pool-status: EU-dedicated: 2 spare racks, US-dedicated: 0, backup-hosted: 6 warm (not reserved).
jules (sales): CloudVendor legal wants the announcement copy to say "preconfigured Dedicated offering" — they will push if we can't guarantee full capacity. we should avoid language that promises specific rack counts.
nina (legal): agree. we can do a joint announcement focused on listing availability and onboarding timeline instead of "reserved capacity guaranteed" language.
sara (procurement): options: (A) ask vendor to reallocate 4 racks from their other manifest (possible but needs expedited freight) (B) borrow 2 racks EU + 2 warm hosted (requires engineering feature flag for routing) (C) delay the live demo announcement until manifests reconcile.
devon (logistics): expediting reallocation costs +$40k and still ~3 day processing. customs could still block.
li (eng-ml): engineering can enable routing to hosted warm nodes with a routing policy flag: ```route_policy: allow-hosted-fallback: true\nimpact: ~15% higher latency 95p``` we can flip the flag in 30–60 min once infra team approves.
marco (partnerships): CloudVendor wants a firm answer in 2 hours. what's low-risk fastest path?
sara (procurement): fastest low-risk is B (2 EU + hosted fallback). I'll draft ask to infra for the routing flag and ping vendor for a temporary copy change.
jules (sales): i'll tell CloudVendor we can proceed with a "preview listing with limited live demo capacity" and that full dedicated capacity will be enforced once all racks arrive — keeps momentum without overpromising.
nina (legal): draft approved. ensure we don't use words like "guaranteed" or "reserved" for the public blurb.
li (eng-ml): tagging infra owners @devops-team — can we get approval to enable allow-hosted-fallback for the CloudVendor listing? (will add tracing & cost tags)
marco (partnerships): thanks — i'll coordinate the message with CloudVendor. sara, devon, please update procurement & logistics runbook for this joint announcement case so we don't scramble next time.
sara (procurement): noted — will create a short playbook entry and link to the manifest/PO check steps.
devon (logistics): will follow up with carrier and vendor for customs docs and ETA push.
marco (partnerships): resolving: B chosen as mitigation. follow-ups: Sara -> playbook, Li -> infra flag, Jules -> vendor message, Devon -> carrier confirmation. I'll post final copy once vendor OKs wording. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: [action-created] #A-3291 enable-hosted-fallback-for-cloudvendor by eng-infra due: 1748014432
marco (partnerships): thanks everyone, i'll update CloudVendor in 90m with our plan.
